summary: The Chip Security Act directs the Department of Commerce to establish security and location-verification requirements for advanced integrated circuit products and computers before they are exported, reexported, or transferred to foreign countries. It also requires individuals and entities authorized to export these products to report any diversion, tampering, or unauthorized locations to the government, and mandates ongoing assessments and reports regarding potential secondary security measures and enforcement authorities.

affected_groups.effect: Must ensure covered integrated circuit products contain location-verification mechanisms and must promptly report any diversion, tampering, or location discrepancies to the Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security.
Tasked with issuing standards, conducting feasibility assessments, reporting to Congress, maintaining product location and end-user records, and executing enforcement and verification authorities.

key_provisions: Requires the Department of Commerce, within 180 days of enactment, to mandate location-verification security mechanisms on covered integrated circuit products prior to foreign export, reexport, or in-country transfer.

Mandates that any person authorized to export covered products under the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 must promptly report if they obtain credible information that a product has been diverted, sent to an unauthorized user, or subjected to tampering.

Requires the Secretary of Commerce to complete an assessment and report to Congress within one year evaluating additional secondary security mechanisms, potential costs, performance impacts, and implementation roadmaps.
Authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to verify ownership and locations of exported covered products, maintain tracking records of products and end-users, and require reporting from license holders.
Requires annual assessments and reports to Congress for three years, starting two years after enactment, on newly developed chip security mechanisms and potential export control adjustments.
missing_information: Specific cost estimates for implementing primary or secondary chip security mechanisms.
Exact technical specifications of future secondary security measures prior to the completion of the Secretary of Commerce's assessment.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Chip Security Act directs the Department of Commerce to establish security and location-verification requirements for advanced integrated circuit products and computers before they are exported, reexported, or transferred to foreign countries. It also requires individuals and entities authorized to export these products to report any diversion, tampering, or unauthorized locations to the government, and mandates ongoing assessments and reports regarding potential secondary security measures and enforcement authorities.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation aims to bolster national security, protect advanced U.S. computing hardware from theft or unauthorized foreign diversion, and enhance compliance with existing export control laws.
